newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks open firmer in directionless trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks open firmer in directionless trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks opened firmer on Tuesday, but the market still lacked direction and red chips had temporarily lost their lustre, brokers said.
"The market has been abandoned by fundamental investors, which makes it very difficult to call it on any given day," said the head of sales at a British brokerage.
The Hang Seng Index was up 67.41 points at 12,677.58 in early trade. Turnover was HK$1.02 billion.
China-related red chips were expected to have a quiet day after profit-taking cooled off the sector in the afternoon session on Monday, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index closed down 35.59 points at 12,610.17 on Monday, but the Dow industrials closed higher overnight, after a three-session losing streak, rising 44.15 points to 6,783.02.
Some red chips, which have surged on speculation that their mainland parents would inject assets into them, were weaker in early trade.
Michael Ng, dealing director with Sassoon Securities, said he expected the market to stay within a relatively narrow range.
"I think the market will be quiet," Ng said.
Apart from red chips, investors were concerned about interest rates, and would be looking at key U.S. economic data this week, brokers said.
U.S. first quarter employment cost index data, a closely watched barometer of wage inflation, is due out on Tuesday, and April employment data is released on Friday.
Brokers also said they expected the expiry of the April index futures contract to have a dampening effect on trading on Tuesday.
Red chips were sold off in early trade, led by Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd, a favourite during the sector's rally.
Shanghai Industrial was off HK$0.80 at HK$44.10, while China Resources Enterprise Ltd tumbled HK$0.85 to HK$21.00.
Blue chips were firmer on the open, led by Hang Seng Bank Ltd and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd.
Hang Seng Bank was up HK$0.75 at HK$86.00, and Henderson Land was up by HK$0.75 at HK$64.75.
Cheung Kong Ltd was also up HK$0.75 at HK$67.75.
HSBC Holdings Plc was up HK$0.50 at HK$189.50.
